n: Full of the Holy Ghost after his baptism, Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness. Being filled with the Spirit doesn’t exempt anyone from trials — it prepares us for them.

f.w: led by the Spirit into the wilderness

n: For forty days he ate nothing, and at the end he was hungry. The JST clarifies that the devil came to tempt him after the forty days, which Jesus had spent communing with God.
The devil’s first temptation targeted physical hunger and questioned his identity: “If you are the Son of God,” turn this stone into bread. Satan often attacks who we are.

f.w: If thou be the Son of God
f.g: The Greek implies “since you are” — tempting him to use his power selfishly.

n: Jesus answered with scripture: people don’t live by bread alone. Spiritual nourishment from God matters more than physical comfort.

f.w: man shall not live by bread alone

n: The devil showed him all the kingdoms of the world in an instant. The JST says it was the Spirit, not the devil, who took Jesus up the mountain.

f.g: In an instant — a visionary view.

n: Satan offered all their power and glory, claiming it had been given to him to hand out. He is a liar; his “gifts” always cost the soul.
The price: worship me, and it will all be yours. A shortcut to a crown that bypassed the cross.
Jesus refused: “Get behind me, Satan.” Scripture says to worship and serve only the Lord God.

f.w: Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God

n: The setting moved to the highest corner of the temple in Jerusalem. If you’re the Son of God, jump. (The JST again has the Spirit bringing Jesus there.)

f.g: A high point of the temple complex, perhaps overlooking the Kidron Valley.

n: This time Satan quoted scripture himself: God will command his angels to protect you. Scripture can be twisted to serve wrong purposes.

f.w: He shall give his angels charge over thee

n: The quote continues: they will carry you so you won’t even hurt your foot on a stone.
Jesus answered with scripture in context: don’t put the Lord your God to the test. Forcing God to prove himself isn’t faith.

f.w: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God

n: When the devil finished every temptation, he left — but only until another opportunity. Temptation returns; resistance must continue.
Jesus returned to Galilee in the Spirit’s power, and news about him spread throughout the region.
He taught in their synagogues, and everyone praised him — at first.
He came to Nazareth, his hometown, and on the sabbath went to the synagogue, as was his habit, and stood up to read. Jesus made regular worship a custom.
He was handed the scroll of Isaiah, unrolled it, and found the passage he wanted.

f.g: A scroll, unrolled to the right place.

n: He read Isaiah 61: the Lord’s Spirit is upon me; he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor, heal broken hearts, free captives, give sight to the blind, and liberate the oppressed. This was his mission statement.

f.w: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me

f.g: The root of “Messiah” and “Christ” — the Anointed One.

n: And to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor — the jubilee, when debts were forgiven and slaves freed.

f.g: A year of God’s favor, echoing the jubilee year of release.

n: He rolled up the scroll, handed it to the attendant, and sat down — the posture of a teacher. Everyone stared at him.

f.g: The synagogue attendant who cared for the scrolls.

n: Then he said: today this scripture is fulfilled as you listen. He was claiming to be the Anointed One Isaiah described.

f.w: This day is this scripture fulfilled

n: At first everyone spoke well of him and marveled at his gracious words, but they asked, “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?” Familiarity began turning to doubt.

f.g: Words full of grace and charm.

n: Jesus knew their thoughts: they would quote the proverb, “Doctor, heal yourself” — prove it by doing the miracles here that you did in Capernaum.

f.g: A proverb challenging him to prove himself at home.

n: He told them plainly that no prophet is accepted in his own hometown.

f.w: No prophet is accepted in his own country

n: He reminded them that in Elijah’s day, during a famine of three and a half years, there were many widows in Israel…
…but Elijah was sent to none of them — only to a Gentile widow in Zarephath, near Sidon.
And in Elisha’s day there were many lepers in Israel, but only Naaman the Syrian — a foreign army commander — was healed. God’s blessings come to those with faith, whatever their nation.
Hearing that God had blessed Gentiles over Israelites, everyone in the synagogue was furious.
They drove him out of town to the edge of the hill Nazareth was built on, intending to throw him off the cliff. The adoring audience became a lynch mob.
But he walked right through the crowd and went on his way. His time to die had not yet come.

f.w: passing through the midst of them

n: He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and taught there on the sabbath.

f.g: A lakeside town lower in elevation than hilly Nazareth — hence “came down.”

n: People were amazed at his teaching, because his message carried authority and power.
In the synagogue, a man possessed by an evil spirit screamed out loudly.
“Leave us alone! What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are — the Holy One of God.” The demon knew exactly who Jesus was.
Jesus rebuked it: “Be quiet and come out!” The demon threw the man down in front of everyone and left without hurting him.
Everyone was amazed: what kind of word is this? With authority and power he commands evil spirits, and they leave!
News about him spread throughout the surrounding area.
Leaving the synagogue, he went to Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law had a high fever, and they asked him to help her. Luke, a physician, notes the fever was “great.”

f.g: A medical term for a severe fever — fitting for Luke, “the beloved physician.”

n: He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left. She got up at once and served them.

f.g: Served them, perhaps preparing a meal.

n: At sunset, when the sabbath ended, people brought all their sick to him. He laid his hands on each one individually and healed them. He ministered one by one.

f.w: laid his hands on every one of them

n: Demons came out of many, shouting, “You are the Christ, the Son of God!” He rebuked them and wouldn’t let them speak, because they knew he was the Messiah.
At daybreak he went to a solitary place. The crowds searched for him and tried to keep him from leaving.
He explained: I must proclaim the good news of God’s kingdom to other towns too — that’s why I was sent.
And he kept preaching in the synagogues of Galilee (some manuscripts read Judea, meaning the Jewish homeland in general).
